references.text: Loose hair was a sign of impurity or shame. The leper was also to have loose hair as a sign of their condition.
The memorial offering (minhat hazikkaron) is mentioned here, where a handful of flour was burned as a memorial offering for the Lord.
Describes how the priest shall take the memorial portion of the grain offering and burn it on the altar.
Earlier in the same chapter, the jealousy offering that a man must bring for his wife is described.
Further describes what the priest shall do with the jealousy offering and the bitter water.
The priest shall take a handful of the offering as a memorial offering and burn it on the altar.
Aaron's sons were forbidden to let their hair hang loose, showing that loose hair was associated with mourning or shame.
The high priest was not to let his hair hang loose, which underscores the significance of loose hair in ritual contexts.
